cues.zh: 简单规则：掌控私钥，比特币才是你的。
cues.en: Simple rule: if you control the keys, it's your bitcoin.

cues.zh: 不掌控私钥，比特币就不是你的。
cues.en: If you don't control the keys, it's not your bitcoin.

cues.zh: 是你的私钥？才是你的比特币。不是你的私钥？就不是你的比特币。
cues.en: Your keys? Your bitcoin. Not your keys? Not your bitcoin.

cues.zh: 是你的私钥？才是你的比特币。不是你的私钥？就不是你的比特币。
cues.en: Your keys? Your bitcoin. Not your keys? Not your bitcoin.

cues.zh: 问题在于：很多人根本不知道该怎么去判断自己到底有没有掌控私钥。
cues.en: Here's the problem: a lot of people have no idea how to even start to decide if they actually control the keys.

cues.zh: 那我来问大家一个问题……
cues.en: So let me ask you a question...

cues.zh: 你们当中有多少人是通过完全掌控私钥，来掌控自己的比特币的？
cues.en: How many of you control your bitcoin with your own control over your keys?

cues.zh: 算我一个。很好……
cues.en: I'm counting myself here. Very good...

cues.zh: 有多少人并没有掌控自己的比特币……
cues.en: How many people do not control their bitcoin...

cues.zh: 而是放在线上账户里的？
cues.en: but have it in an online account?

cues.zh: 或者是由别人代为掌管比特币的？
cues.en: Or somebody else is controlling the bitcoin?

cues.zh: 别害羞！没关系的，我们都是这么过来的。好……
cues.en: Don't be shy! It's okay, we all started there. Okay...

cues.zh: 更重要的是，有多少人根本不知道该怎么回答这个问题？
cues.en: More importantly, how many people have no idea how to answer that question?

cues.zh: 你并不知道自己是否掌控它，对吧？
cues.en: You don't know if you control it, right?

cues.zh: 好，那我给你一些建议。
cues.en: Okay, so let me give you some advice.

cues.zh: 如果你用的钱包，每次交易都会生成一个新地址，
cues.en: If you are running a wallet where, each time you do a transaction, it generates a new address,

cues.zh: 但你刚开始用那个钱包时，它让你记下类似“写下这十二个词……”或者
cues.en: ... but when you started using that wallet, it told you something like "Write down these twelve words..." or

cues.zh: “这二十四个词，保存好作为备份。”
cues.en: "these twenty-four words, and keep them as a backup."

cues.zh: 那些词？它们能生成你所有的密钥。
cues.en: Those words? They generate all your keys.

cues.zh: 你必须把它们写下来做备份，是因为你掌控着那些密钥。
cues.en: The reason you have to write them as a backup is because you are controlling those keys.

cues.zh: 如果你丢了那些词，你就丢了密钥和比特币。
cues.en: If you lose those words, you lose the keys & the bitcoin.

cues.zh: 能力越大，责任越大。
cues.en: With great power comes great responsibility.

cues.zh: 如果你的钱包要求你写下备份，那说明你掌控着密钥。
cues.en: If you have a wallet in which you were asked to write down the backup, you control the keys.

cues.zh: 如果你没写下备份，
cues.en: If you didn't write down the backup,

cues.zh: 那今晚回家就是个好时机，
cues.en: when you go home tonight would be a good time

cues.zh: 打开设置，找到“备份”，在你弄丢手机之前，把那该死的十二个词写下来……
cues.en: to open the settings, go to "Backup," and write down those damn twelve words before you lose your phone...

cues.zh: 或者上厕所发短信，手一滑掉马桶里了。大家都干过这事……
cues.en: or drop it in the toilet because you were trying to text while in the bathroom. We all do it...

cues.zh: 掉进马桶后手机报废，你的比特币也就跟着没了，那接下来怎么办？
cues.en: You dropped it in the toilet and your bitcoin disappeared because your phone blew up, and then what?

cues.zh: 给“比特币客服中心”打电话？
cues.en: You call the "Bitcoin help desk"?

cues.zh: 根本就没有“比特币客服中心”。
cues.en: There is no "Bitcoin help desk."

cues.zh: 你跑去 Reddit 上发帖：“我私钥丢了！求求谁能帮帮我？”
cues.en: You go on Reddit and [say], "I lost my keys! Please, can someone help me?"

cues.zh: 大家会怎么回你？
cues.en: And what are people going to say?

cues.zh: “你记下那12个助记词了吗？没记？”
cues.en: Did you write down the twelve words? You didn't?

cues.zh: “节哀顺变吧……”
cues.en: Sorry for your loss...

cues.zh: 好吧……那该怎么做备份呢？
cues.en: All right... How do you know how to do a backup?

cues.zh: 又该怎么掌控自己的私钥？
cues.en: How to control your own [keys]?

cues.zh: 很多人都不知道从何下手，所以我要给大家做个非常简短的小教程，
cues.en: A lot of people don't know how to start, so I'm going to give you a very quick, little tutorial

cues.zh: 讲讲如何掌控自己的私钥。准备好了吗？
cues.en: on how to control your own keys. Okay?

cues.zh: 首先，你手头最安全的设备是什么？
cues.en: First of all, what is the most secure device you own?

cues.zh: 不是你的笔记本！绝对不是你的笔记本。
cues.en: Not your laptop! Definitely not your laptop.

cues.zh: 在场有多少人用 Windows？
cues.en: How many here have Windows?

cues.zh: 我深表同情……
cues.en: My sincere condolences...

cues.zh: 你的 Windows 电脑不属于你，而是被一群人控制着
cues.en: You don't own your Windows machines. Your Windows machines are owned by a combination

cues.zh: 他们是病毒和木马，还有远在世界另一端的俄罗斯和中国黑客。
cues.en: of viruses and trojans, that are controlled by Russian and Chinese hackers somewhere else in the world.

cues.zh: 那根本不是你的电脑。他们只是偶尔让你用一下。别在那些设备上存比特币。
cues.en: They're not really your machines. They just let you use them occasionally. Do not put bitcoin on those devices.

cues.zh: 那就像是在给黑客捐钱。
cues.en: That's like making a donation to hackers.

cues.zh: 他们的程序会主动搜索比特币软件；一旦找到，就会把它拿走。或者他们会装键盘记录器……
cues.en: They have software actively looking for Bitcoin software; when they find it, they take it. Or they put a key logger...

cues.zh: 等你进行交易、输入密码，
cues.en: wait for you to do a transaction, enter your password,

cues.zh: 然后他们就把钱拿走。
cues.en: and then they take it.

cues.zh: 你拥有的最安全的设备是智能手机。
cues.en: The most secure device you own is your smartphone.

cues.zh: Android、iOS？这是你拥有的最安全的设备。
cues.en: Android, iOS? It's the most secure device you own.

cues.zh: 智能手机上的操作系统比笔记本电脑和台式机上的安全得多，尤其是 Windows。
cues.en: Operating systems on smartphones are far more secure than laptops and desktops, especially Windows.

cues.zh: 你的智能手机可能是存放钱包的最佳选择。
cues.en: Your smartphone is probably the best place to run a wallet.

cues.zh: 如果你在加密货币上投了很多钱，或者持有很多比特币……
cues.en: if you have a lot of money invested in cryptocurrencies, or own a lot of bitcoin...

cues.zh: “很多”对不同的人来说意思不一样，但如果你觉得这算“很多”……
cues.en: The word "a lot" means different things to different people, but if you feel like it's "a lot"...

cues.zh: 如果我现在告诉你，你的比特币刚被盗了，你会说：“哦……我再买一些”吗？
cues.en: If right now I told you your bitcoin has just been stolen, do you [say], "Eh... I'll get some more"?

cues.zh: 还是会哭出来？
cues.en: Or do you start crying?

cues.zh: 还是得跟父母和配偶进行一场非常艰难的谈话，
cues.en: Or do you have to have a very difficult conversation with your parents and your spouse

cues.zh: 解释为什么孩子上不了大学？
cues.en: about why your kids won't be going to college?

cues.zh: 这就是加密货币“很多”这个说法的不同含义，对吧？
cues.en: Those are the variations in the word "a lot" of [cryptocurrency], right?

cues.zh: 如果你持有很多加密货币，多到丢了会让你难受，
cues.en: If you have a lot of [cryptocurrency], more than what you would be upset to lose,

cues.zh: 那你就该买个硬件钱包。
cues.en: you should buy a hardware wallet.

cues.zh: 硬件钱包是一种 USB 设备。我推荐几款：Ledger、Trezor，都很不错。
cues.en: A hardware wallet is a USB device. I can recommend a couple of those: Ledger, Trezor. Those are really good.

cues.zh: *BitcoinTrezor.com（现为 Trezor.io）、LedgerWallet.com、KeepKey……还有不少其他选择。
cues.en: *BitcoinTrezor.com (now Trezor.io), LedgerWallet.com, KeepKey... there's a bunch of others.

cues.zh: 现在买起来有点困难，因为似乎有一百万人发现了
cues.en: They're a bit difficult to buy right now, because apparently about a million people noticed

cues.zh: 比特币价格涨了，决定终于来试试这东西，于是出门去买硬件钱包，
cues.en: that the bitcoin price went up, decided to finally join this thing, then went out and tried to buy a hardware wallet,

cues.zh: 结果都卖光了。这倒是个好问题。
cues.en: so they're out of stock. That's a good problem to have.

cues.zh: 硬件钱包是一个小型 USB 设备，可以把你的比特币密钥保存在高度安全的专用设备上。
cues.en: A hardware wallet is a little USB device which keeps your bitcoin keys on a highly secure, special purpose device.

cues.zh: 即使你的电脑里塞满了病毒和黑客程序，你也能安全地使用这个设备，
cues.en: Even if your computer is absolutely full of viruses and hackers, you can use that device securely

cues.zh: 因为所有操作都在设备上完成，而且设备本身不会通过 USB 遭到攻击。
cues.en: because everything happens on the device, and the device itself can't be attacked over USB.

cues.zh: 否则几乎不可能。
cues.en: Or it's almost impossible.

cues.zh: 所以，买一个硬件钱包。如果买不了硬件钱包，就在智能手机上下载软件。
cues.en: So, buy a hardware wallet. If you can't buy a hardware wallet, download software onto your smartphone.

cues.zh: 如果你用iOS，我可以推荐Breadwallet、Mycelium、Copay或Airbitz。
cues.en: If you have iOS, I could recommend Breadwallet, Mycelium, Copay, or Airbitz.

cues.zh: 如果你用安卓[手机]：Mycelium、Copay或Airbitz。
cues.en: If you have an Android [phone]: Mycelium, Copay, or Airbitz.

cues.zh: 我不为这些公司工作，也没拿过这些公司的钱。
cues.en: I don't work for any of these companies, and I haven't taken money from any of these companies.

cues.zh: 它们只是我用过的；它们已经存在一段时间了，我相信它们比
cues.en: They are just ones that I've used; they've been around for a while, I trust them to be much better than

cues.zh: 你现在用的任何其他东西都要好得多。
cues.en: whatever else you are doing right now.

cues.zh: 下载那些钱包，安装到你的智能手机上，然后当它提示你
cues.en: Download those wallets, install them on your smartphone, and then when it tells you to

cues.zh: 备份你的十二到二十四个英文单词时——别自作聪明，别玩花样。
cues.en: make a backup of your twelve to twenty-four English words -- don't get smart, don't get fancy.

cues.zh: 别说：“那好，我把三个词写在这儿……”
cues.en: Don't say, "Well, I'll write three of the words here..."

cues.zh: “……然后我把另外三个词倒序排列，存进通讯录，藏在书房里……”
cues.en: "... and then I'll take the other three words, reverse them, put them in my phone book, hide them in my library...."

cues.zh: “……再交给我表弟——”别耍小聪明！
cues.en: "...give them to my cousin-" Don't get fancy!

cues.zh: 纸和笔。老老实实记下这 12 到 24 个词。
cues.en: Paper, pencil. Write down the 12-24 words.

cues.zh: 别人拿到这几张纸还能认出它是什么的概率？微乎其微。
cues.en: The chances that someone is going to get hold of that and know what it is? Pretty slim.

cues.zh: 放进抽屉锁好。或者放进保险箱锁好。
cues.en: Put it in a drawer, lock it. Put it in the safe, lock it.

cues.zh: 然后你就可以正常用手机了。手机丢了，你还有助记词。助记词丢了，
cues.en: Then you can use your phone. If you lose your phone, you have the words. If you lose the words,

cues.zh: 你还有手机。两者效果等同。随时都能用这些词恢复钱包。你所有的交易记录、
cues.en: you have your phone. Both are equivalent. Any time you want, restore from those words. All of your transactions,

cues.zh: 你所有的钱，全都能找回来。
cues.en: all of your money, you get back.

cues.zh: 现在你的加密货币全由你自己掌控了。
cues.en: Now you control your cryptocurrency.

cues.zh: 这类钱包有很多——比如 Jaxx 也是一个，适合持有多种加密货币而不只是比特币的人。
cues.en: These wallets, many of them- Jaxx is another one, if you have multiple currencies and not just bitcoin.

cues.zh: 如果你有以太坊、Dash、Monero、Zcash、LTC 等等。
cues.en: If you have ether, Dash, Monero, Zcash, LTC, whatever.

cues.zh: Jaxx。J-A-X-X。
cues.en: Jaxx. J-A-X-X.

cues.zh: Exodus？
cues.en: Exodus?

cues.zh: Exodus？
cues.en: Exodus?

cues.zh: 没听说过。我不知道它是不是……
cues.en: Never heard of it. I don't know if it's-

cues.zh: 这并不意味着它不好。
cues.en: That doesn't mean it's not good.

cues.zh: 我只是说我个人没听说过。好吧……
cues.en: I'm just saying I haven't personally heard about it. Okay...

cues.zh: 下载这类钱包中的一个。用铅笔把助记词写在纸上，懂吗？如果我们的文明明天终结，
cues.en: Download one of those wallets. Write down the phrases, pencil on paper, right? If our civilization ended tomorrow,

cues.zh: 一个月……两个月内，所有的 CD、DVD、硬盘、U盘都会化为灰烬。
cues.en: in one month... two months, all of the CDs, DVDs, hard drives, USB drives, would be dust.

cues.zh: 好吧，也许撑不到三个月。但三千年后呢？全成灰了。而我们现在还能找到埃及人的纸！
cues.en: Okay, maybe not three months. But three thousand years? Dust. We're still finding paper from the Egyptians!

cues.zh: 纸能保存很久，对吧？写在纸上。别放在 U 盘里。纸。普通的无酸纸可以保存
cues.en: Paper lasts, yes? Paper. Don't put it on a USB drive. Paper. Simple, acid-free paper will last for

cues.zh: 数百年；如果你格外小心谨慎，还可以把它过塑，这样就不会被水损坏。
cues.en: hundreds of years; if you're extra paranoid, you laminate it so that it cannot get destroyed by water.

cues.zh: 你从办公用品店买一个非常便宜的防火保险箱，把东西放进去，这样就不会被烧毁。
cues.en: You buy a very inexpensive, fire-proof safe from your office store. You put it inside so it can't be burned.

cues.zh: 洪水、火灾、盗窃……全都覆盖！
cues.en: Flood, fire, theft... covered!

cues.zh: 现在在这种系统上——钱包、带备份助记词的硬件钱包——你可以存储……
cues.en: Now on that kind of system -- of wallets, hardware wallets with your backup words -- you can store...

cues.zh: ……我认识一些人在这种系统上存了数百万美元（我没开玩笑）。
cues.en: ... I know people who store millions of dollars (I'm not joking) on exactly that kind of of system.

cues.zh: 一旦你掌控了自己的比特币，分叉就无所谓了，你的交易所决定
cues.en: Once you have control of your bitcoin, it doesn't matter if there's a fork, it doesn't matter if your exchange decides

cues.zh: 走哪条路也无所谓。都无所谓。你不该把钱放在那个交易所里。
cues.en: to go one way or another. It doesn't matter. You should not be keeping your money on that exchange.

cues.zh: 你不该把钱交给别人、信任别人替你保管安全。
cues.en: You should not be keeping your money [by trusting] someone else to keep it safe for you.

cues.zh: 那不过就是个银行。我们做这个开放区块链的部分原因，就是因为我们不信任银行。
cues.en: That's just a bank. Part of the reason we're doing this open blockchain is because we don't trust banks.
